sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-HA immunofluorescence confirmed surface expression; receptor-mediated signal transduction, protein–protein interactions, and subcellular localization were all studied via the HA handle (L4). Separately, N-terminal FLAG-δR was 'extensively confirmed' to be functional across multiple labs and assays including agonist-induced endocytosis and G-protein signalling (L6, L12).
sites.rationale: OPRD1 has no signal peptide; the N-terminus (residues 1–48) is entirely extracellular and 48 residues from the first TM helix (TM1 begins at residue 49), giving ample clearance for a short epitope tag. 'Inserted immediately before the ORF' unambiguously places the tag before Met1, i.e. insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M. Python verification confirms seq[0] = 'M' and the 48-residue extracellular span. Four independent publications using HA, FLAG, and GFP tags at this exact junction, with surface display and functional assays confirmed, make this the highest-confidence site in the ledger. Knock-in mice were generated at the endogenous OPRD1 locus (TALEN-assisted) with an HA-tag inserted 'immediately before the ORF' of the DOR gene, producing a full-length N-terminally HA-tagged receptor expressed from the native promoter. The same N-terminal prepend topology is independently corroborated by N-terminally FLAG-tagged δR in PC12/HEK293 cells (PMC5531736), N-terminally Flag-tagged DOR in Neuro2A and CHO cells (PMC9043031), and FLAG-FDOR in a fourth study (PMC10154970).

sources.claim: An HA-tag sequence was inserted right before the ORF of DOR gene to allow the expression of an HA-DOR N-terminal fusion.

literature_notes: All twelve ledger lines describe the identical junction: an N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue = 0) on full-length, membrane-anchored OPRD1. L1–L4 (PMC5353682) use an HA knock-in at the endogenous locus; L5–L9 (PMC5531736) use N-terminal FLAG and GFP in PC12/HEK293 cells; L10–L11 (PMC9043031) use N-terminal Flag in Neuro2A and CHO cells; L12 (PMC10154970) uses N-terminal FLAG (FDOR) for endocytosis tracking. No ledger line names any residue in ECL1 (108–122), ECL2 (189–211), or ECL3 (284–297), so no internal sites are proposed. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are reported in the ledger.
